subject.title: [Security] Unauthenticated local tool endpoint exposure in openclaw-tools-serve.ts

question: Does the reporter have a reproducible unauthenticated HTTP tool-invocation path outside the named MCP stdio files, or should this report close as non-reproducible?
rationale: The current source disproves an HTTP listener in the named files, but the protected security label and existence of separate Gateway tool surfaces require a human security-boundary decision before cleanup.

options.title: Request exact endpoint proof
options.body: Ask for the process command, listening address and port, complete redacted HTTP request, response, and tool side effect on current main before choosing a fix owner.

options.title: Close named report
options.body: Close as non-reproducible if no separate endpoint evidence is provided, because the named implementations are stdio child-process servers.

options.title: Route distinct Gateway report
options.body: If the evidence targets Gateway `/tools/invoke`, assess it separately against Gateway authentication and owner-only authorization rather than modifying the MCP bridge.

recommendation.title: Request exact endpoint proof
recommendation.body: Ask for the process command, listening address and port, complete redacted HTTP request, response, and tool side effect on current main before choosing a fix owner.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work directly covered the adjacent Gateway HTTP/RPC tool authorization boundary implicated if the reporter named the wrong files.
